pr_title: Make label templates have consistent behavior and priority
pr_body:
Fix https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/issues/23715

Other related PRs:

* #23717
* #23716
* #23719

This PR is different from others, it tries to resolve the problem fundamentally (and brings more benefits)

Although it looks like some more lines are added, actually many new lines are for tests.

----

Before, the code was just "guessing" the file type and try to parse them.


<details>

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2114189/228002245-57d58e27-1078-4da9-bf42-5bc0b264c6ce.png)

</details>


This PR:

* Always remember the original option file names, and always use correct parser for them.

* Another benefit is that we can sort the Label Templates now (before there was a map, its key order is undefined)

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2114189/228002432-931b9f18-3908-484b-a36b-04760c9ad132.png)

As I explained on my PR - loadRepoConfig is run once and once only.

This PR would prevent users from being able to drop in a new custom labels file to override the inbuilt one unless it had the same extension as the one in `options` or builtin.
It would be possible to add back in the functionality that this PR breaks (and in fact allow for labels etc to be truly reloadable whilst gitea is running) is we were to add in an fsnotify handler.

> As I explained on my PR - loadRepoConfig is run once and once only.
> 
> This PR would prevent users from being able to drop in a new custom labels file to override the inbuilt one unless it had the same extension as the one in `options` or builtin.

> It would be possible to add back in the functionality that this PR breaks (and in fact allow for labels etc to be truly reloadable whilst gitea is running) is we were to add in an fsnotify handler.

Why? In production, I do not see why a site admin expects to add/remove files without restarting the server.

I guess zeripath meant:

1. Gitea have a builtin "Default".
2. Then a site admin drops a "Default.yaml" into custom template directory.

In my mind, in this case, the site admin should restart Gitea, just like they drops a "NewLabels.yaml"

@wxiaoguang the problem with passing the filename to the UI is that it is fundamentally the wrong thing.

Users are NOT choosing a file for the labels - they're choosing a label-set.
I fundamentally disagree with this approach. It is incorrect and it is establishing that the label-set is the filename.

I definitely think this approach is a correct one.

`MyLabel.yaml` and `MyLabel.yml` are different label sets


I do not know why we should waste time on it, I never see a real bad case from you. Please show a real case how this approach would hurt end users if you really think this PR is wrong.

1. MyLabels
2. MyLabels
3. MyLabels

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2114189/228595346-311842b8-fc30-4fc0-bb4b-75a94e832dd2.png)

Commit 964d81b0bece7db9d86e9b78f586aab3fd1ceeef addresses the concern from zeripath about "breaking". Now, since we only have one name for each label sets, we can safely always use the DisplayName.

And, it does some refactroing and fixes some legacy bugs like: `ErrTemplateLoad{TemplateFile: labelName, errors.New("label name and color are required fields")}`. So the new variables all have clear names.

Summary: now the new behavior is:

1. Collect all label template files (builtin and custom)
2. Merge them with priority (the priority logic is covered by tests)
    * custom > builtin,  yaml > yml > no-ext
    * No duplicate items, as before
3. Use a DisplayName => FileName map to keep the real file names used for display names
    * Users/API calls always use DisplayName (`Advanced`), as before
4. Other necessary refactoring and bug fixes

I do not see a reason why Gitea should support the behavior you described. Your PR doesn't support dropping in everything. For example:

* The builtin are `Advanced.yaml` and `Default`
* User starts Gitea
* User drops `Advance.yml` and `MyLables.yml`
* User tries to create a repo:
    * Your PR: the user sees new `Advanced`, old `Default`, no `MyLables` (surprise: new/old/no).
    * My PR: the user sees old `Advanced`, old `Default`, no `MyLables`
        * If the user drops in `Advanced.yaml`, or edits the one already exists, it still takes affect, as before.

There is no much difference indeed.

In the end, the user must restart Gitea, while my PR is more clear to to the user: you must resart Gitea to make the lables take affect.


And about "whereas previously this just worked": I never consider it as a reason if there is no real requirement. I have changed many Gitea's behaviors, I believe many changes help to reduce bug reports.

Although, loading them into memory and not doing FS operations each time they are requested would alleviate some (probably non-measurable) pressure from the disk.

Agree, this PR doesn't break. Some unclear old behaviors are just undocumented / done by accident, such old behaviors shouldn't block new necessary changes.

Yup, if we want to support such behavior, then we need a clear definition, especially for newly added files, neither my PR nor zeripath's PR supports it now.

For my PR, there is no blocker for supporting the reloading (no-restart) behavior: just refresh the global LabelTemplateFiles variables.

issue_context.title: custom label option appears twice
issue_context.body:
### Description

when adding a custom yaml label file, an option appears twice. the glob appears to be searching for files as well as file types 

### Gitea Version

1.19.0

### Can you reproduce the bug on the Gitea demo site?

No

### Log Gist

_No response_

### Screenshots

![2023-03-26_14-03-1679838041](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4564448/227779682-82a66529-6caa-465b-8557-ecab32a93872.jpg)


```
#pwd
/var/lib/gitea/custom/options/label

#ls
test.yaml

#cat test.yaml
labels:
  - name: "foo/bar"  # name of the label that will appear in the dropdown
    exclusive: true # whether to use the exclusive namespace for scoped labels. scoped delimiter is /
    color: aabbcc # hex colour coding
    description: Some label # long description of label intent
  - name: "foo/baz"  # name of the label that will appear in the dropdown
    exclusive: true # whether to use the exclusive namespace for scoped labels. scoped delimiter is /
    color: aabbcc # hex colour coding
    description: Some other label # long description of label intent
```

### Git Version

2.40.0

### Operating System

linux (gentoo)

### How are you running Gitea?

rc-service 

### Database

None
